correctness.rationale: Exact hyperbolic area follows from v=u/(1-u). Normalized monomial spectrum and incomplete beta recurrence yield a simple isolated top eigenvalue and gaps (1-u)^a B_m. Differentiating the compactly supported Toeplitz family in trace norm, the simple eigenvalue second-derivative formula gives the complete coefficient including its positive eigenvector-response denominator. The finite-binomial differential identity P_m=a u+(1-u)Σ(m+1-k)b_k>0 proves strict q_m ordering, and m=2 evaluates to (2-u)/(2+(a+1)u). A numerical weighted finite-section check reproduced the predicted mixed-harmonic coefficient with relative error falling from about 4.2e-3 to 1.6e-5. Numeric checks are corroboration only; analytic steps cover all a,H>0 and fixed real C² mean-zero h.

originality.rationale: The fixed-domain principal-eigenvalue second shape derivative and its exact ordered multiplier spectrum are distinct from Ramos–Tilli global disk optimality and from the 2024 functional-variation Hessian for jointly optimized superlevel regions. The latter has W_k but not the inverse disk spectral-gap factor B_k in the present coefficient. The Gaussian/Fock shape result uses a different operator and Euclidean rather than hyperbolic measure. Targeted indexed searches and accessible related records found no exact or stronger all-parameter hyperbolic domain-shape spectrum. Residual historical-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Historical priority cannot be proved by search; an unindexed manuscript might have computed the same fixed-domain Hessian.

value.rationale: A quantitatively exact local Hessian of the optimized Cauchy-wavelet localization eigenvalue resolves the stability profile of the domain mask itself under an invariant area constraint, distinguishes genuine hyperbolic translations from angular distortions, and identifies the globally sharp frequency-two curvature within the local Hessian for every positive weight and disk area. This local spectral curvature is not supplied by disk-optimality or nonoptimal global asymmetry bounds, and is motivated by robustness of concentration against area-preserving mask errors.
